question: On 21 June 2022, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) rendered its judgment on the PNR Directive1 and set strict limitations for the Member States regarding the application of the Directive, thereby significantly narrowing the ways in which they may process passenger name record data. Against this background: 1.

Can the Commission provide an overview of the compatibility of the application of the PNR Directive in the Member States with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU, in particular with the fundamental right to protection of personal data, as well as an overview of all (legislative) measures taken or planned in the Member States to effectively protect the fundamental rights of passengers?
What precise actions has the Commission taken to ensure that each Member State’s respective national implementation and application of the PNR Directive are in line with the Charter?

In which Member States are the implementation and application of the PNR Directive not in line with the Charter, and will the Commission start infringement proceedings against these Member States? If not, why not?

Directive (EU) 2016/681 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the use of passenger name record (PNR) data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime (OJ L 119, 4.5.2016, p. 132).
answer: The Commission welcomes that the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) in its Judgment of 22 June 2022 has confirmed the validity of the Passenger Name Record (PNR) Directive provided that its provisions are interpreted in consistency with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU (2).

With a focus on the effects of the CJEU ruling, discussions on the application of the PNR Directive have continued in different fora, such as the dedicated bi-annual meetings with representatives of the Member States organised by the Commission and the competent Council working groups.

In these discussions, the Commission has supported Member States in their efforts to take a consistent approach on operationalising the new CJEU requirements and, where necessary, launching internal processes to adjust their PNR legislation and/or PNR systems in accordance with the CJEU interpretations.

The Commission is focusing its continued efforts to monitor the implementation and application of the PNR Directive on compliance with the CJEU interpretations. On this basis, it will consider the most appropriate course of action, including the launch of infringement proceedings for cases of non-conformity.

Directive (EU) 2016/681 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the use of passenger name record (PNR) data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime (OJ L 119, 4.5.2016, p. 132).
